title: This Bird Flew 100 Miles Without Flapping Its Wings Once

scenes.text: This bird flew over a hundred miles without flapping once.
It's an Andean condor. One bird stayed in the air for five hours without a single wingbeat.
Scientists put sensors on wild condors and tracked every flap.
Across all their flights, they flapped just one percent of the time.
Most of that was taking off. After that, they ride rising warm air.
A bird that weighs up to 33 pounds, surfing the sky. One percent flapping.

description:
Andean condors flap their wings for only about 1 percent of their flying time.
A 2020 study that tracked wild condors found one bird flew for five hours, covering more than 100 miles, without a single wingbeat. Most of the flapping happened at take-off, after which the birds rode rising air. Condors weigh up to about 15 kilograms.
Would you rather glide or run? Comment below.
first_comment: That's about 172 kilometres on one glide. How long could you hold your arms out?
